text:
Lauren Bishop: looping in runtime folks — we need to align on how we message performance profile changes to Dedicated customers for runtime-1.22.

Specifically:
1) what do we say changes *when* profile defaults update (H100/L40S now, B200 later)
2) what do we expose in Console vs keep as “support/debug only”

I’m worried about customers interpreting “profile change” as “you changed my infra under me” and asking for SLA guarantees.

Mateo Alvarez: +1, we should be very crisp. Dedicated should not feel like Hosted roulette.

Noah Patel: agreed. From runtime POV: the profile pack is basically a versioned set of safe runtime defaults keyed off SKU + driver/CUDA + workload bucket. We can summarize as “performance tuning settings” without getting into every knob.

Sofia Ivanova: on the scheduler side, most changes are about queue policy + batching heuristics for mixed workloads. We should avoid promising “always faster”, but can say “reduces tail latency regressions and improves predictability across prompt shapes”.

Lauren Bishop: ok. what’s the minimum set of “facts” we should put in customer-facing comms?

Hiro Tanaka: for kernel: I *really* don’t want to expose kernel variant names (e.g. attention v3) in Console. Customers will cargo-cult and ask to pin “v3” even when it’s wrong for their driver/context length. Better to expose a stable profile version string.

Allison Grant: re Console: we can show:
- GPU SKU (they already know)
- active profile_id + profile_version
- last change timestamp / runtime version
- a link to “what this means” doc

But avoid listing dozens of tuning fields. That can live in an internal debug bundle.

Connor O'Brien: release engineering angle: we need a changelog discipline. If profile defaults change in 1.22.x we should call it out in release notes (even if runtime code doesn’t change much). Otherwise customer sees p95 move and thinks we hid it.

Paula Mendes: also want clear wording on control: “you can pin a profile version” and “rollback is supported”. The *how* (support ticket vs self-serve) can vary by customer maturity.

Lauren Bishop: on pinning: do we want to say “available by request” or actually put a toggle in Console?

Noah Patel: near term: I’d keep pinning as “supported via support / CSM” for Dedicated, at least initially. We have guardrails + audit logging, but we don’t want customers randomly pinning older versions and then blaming us for missing fixes.

Kira Thompson: +1 — from docs/runbook side: we can document the pin + rollback path and set expectations: pin is for stability during investigations / planned launches, not the default operating mode.

Elliot Price: customer docs should say:
- what a “profile” is (versioned performance defaults)
- what triggers changes (runtime upgrade, or a targeted profile update)
- what we watch (latency percentiles, error rates, OOM)
- what customers can do (monitor, pin, request change)

And then point to SKU-specific “expected behavior” tables without dumping raw benchmark matrices.

Lauren Bishop: can we agree on what to expose in Console *now* for v1? DES is asking for “minimum viable UI”.

Allison Grant: proposal for v1 Console (debug view only, not main dashboard):
- “Runtime performance profile: <profile_id> (<profile_version>)”
- “Detected hardware: H100-SXM / L40S / etc”
- “Compatibility: OK / WARNING (driver mismatch)”

Everything else stays internal. We can also add a “copy diagnostics” button that includes profile + sku.

Hiro Tanaka: compatibility status is good. If it’s WARNING, that’s actionable without showing kernel internals.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. Also add “scheduling mode” (mixed vs decode-priority) maybe? but if that’s too in-the-weeds, keep it internal.

Mateo Alvarez: let’s keep it simple. For messaging:
- We’re introducing versioned performance profiles per GPU
- Updates are staged + SLO-guardrailed
- Dedicated can opt-in / pin during rollout windows
- We will call out changes in release notes

No promises like “always faster”; instead “predictable and observable”.

Lauren Bishop: wording check — can we say: “Profile updates may change latency/throughput characteristics; we validate against acceptance thresholds and will rollback if SLOs degrade”?

Noah Patel: yes, but add: “within expected behavior ranges per SKU/workload bucket”. Otherwise people ask “define degrade”.

Connor O'Brien: and we should say how we communicate: “we’ll include the profile version in the runtime upgrade notes” + “support can confirm active profile”.

Paula Mendes: action items?

Lauren Bishop: action items:
- I’ll update PM-881 messaging draft w/ agreed bullets + pin/rollback language.
- Allison: confirm exact Console fields for DES-214 (profile_id, profile_version, sku, compatibility status).
- Noah/Mateo: send me 2-3 sentences on “why profiles exist” that don’t mention kernels.
- Connor: ensure runtime-1.22 notes include “profile pack enabled + how to find active profile version”.

Mateo Alvarez: :thumbsup: will DM copy.

Allison Grant: :eyes: on DES-214; I’ll post a screenshot mock later today.

Hiro Tanaka: thanks. pls no “kernel v3” in any customer doc 🙏

Lauren Bishop: lol understood. :white_check_mark:
